shouldFix.title: D-135-SF-1 is recorded ACCEPTED but only half performed, and the missing half is what adjudicates the other reviewer's contradictory count
shouldFix.finding: The disposition table records D-135-SF-1 as ACCEPTED. The turn-1 repair had two parts: replace '63 rows' with '65 rows', AND state the composition so the figure is re-derivable by the next act that adds a row. Only the first landed. Neither '12 + 30 + 5 + 16' nor any derivation of 65 appears anywhere in the entry. That gap now matters more than it did at turn 1, because the other turn-1 reviewer published a contradictory measurement in a frozen verdict: Codex advisory D135-A1 states that 'direct table-row counting yields 69 before D-135 and 71 after' and recommends correcting the preamble to 71. The entry adopts 65, never mentions 71, and does not dispose D135-A1 — it is absent from the disposition table, and the string D135-A1 occurs zero times in the subject. I resolved the conflict empirically rather than by preferring my own count: git log -S located commit b9c2490, the commit that introduced the phrase, and at that commit the row classes were inherited 12, V2 30, five-review 5, DR-011 residuals 16, gates 22 — identical to today. Only 12 + 30 + 5 + 16 = 63 reproduces the written figure; 69, 47 and 85 do not. The composition excludes the gate table and includes the DR-011 residual subledger, the figure was exact when written, and 65 is correct. So the entry writes the right number — but on adoption the corpus would carry an authoritative 65 alongside a frozen reviewer verdict asserting 71, with nothing on the record adjudicating between them, and with no derivation for the next act that adds a row.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 non-blocking advisory. Nineteen attacks run, three landed on one blocking finding and one advisory. Custody is intact: turn-2 subject e7ad37b6 at 0444 unmoved, turn-1 subject frozen at ec908ac5, HEAD never left d3a3b74, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all seven measured-inputs rows reproduce. Three of the four accepted repairs landed whole. My SF-2 landed and I verified it hard: the relative link resolves, D-134's two CONSENT digests recompute from the verdict files and match the digests the adopted D-134 entry itself cites, and D-132 is correctly cited by commit rather than CONSENT because it was user-made with no reviewer verdicts — a distinction handled correctly and unprompted. What blocks is that my SF-1 is recorded ACCEPTED but performed in half. The 63→65 byte edit landed; the composition statement did not. That gap matters more now than at turn 1 because Codex's frozen turn-1 advisory D135-A1 asserts the figure should be 71, and this entry adopts 65 without mentioning it — D135-A1 appears zero times in the subject. I resolved the disagreement empirically rather than by preferring my own count: at commit b9c2490, which introduced the phrase, the row classes were 12 / 30 / 5 / 16 / 22, and only 12 + 30 + 5 + 16 = 63 reproduces the written figure, so the composition excludes gates and includes the DR-011 residuals and 65 is right. The entry writes the correct number; it just does not show the derivation or answer the reviewer who measured differently, so adoption would leave an unadjudicated numeric conflict on the record. Two sentences fix it. My caution to the coordinator is explicit: do not switch 65 to 71 — the repair is to record why 65 is correct.
